properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Kansas...

Big Blue River near Blue Rapids affecting Marshall County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Big Blue River near Blue Rapids.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 26.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding occurs from
Marysville to Tuttle Creek Lake.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 AM CDT Tuesday the stage was 30.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Thursday morning and continue falling to 19.5 feet Sunday
morning.
- Flood stage is 26.0 feet.
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

available at www.weather.gov/top/.

properties.areaDesc: Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 6 at 8:57AM EDT until October 6 at 12:00PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until noon EDT.

* At 857 AM EDT, thunderstorms capable of producing waterspouts were
located along a line extending from near S Tower to 43 nm south of
V Tower, moving northeast at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
S Tower, V Tower, and Buckeye Reef.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.areaDesc: Duval, FL
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 6 at 8:51AM EDT until October 6 at 10:45AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...East Central Duval County in northeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 1045 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas. Ponding of water in urban or other
areas is occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 851 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Minor flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.
Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Jacksonville Beach, Atlantic Beach and Neptune Beach.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

reflective clothing and carry a light to increase your visibility
to drivers.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 6 at 7:40AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor has risen into Minor Flood Stage and is
forecast to continue a steady rise through this week due to northerly
winds and repeated rounds of heavy rainfall across the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...From this morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 2.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:30 AM EDT Tuesday was 2.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river has risen to Minor Flood Stage at 2.3 feet
and is expected to continue rising through flood stage, reaching
2.7 feet late this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.6
feet on 10/14/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Bryan; Coastal Chatham; Coastal Liberty; Coastal McIntosh; Beaufort; Coastal Colleton; Charleston; Coastal Jasper
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 6 at 7:00AM EDT until October 6 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 6 feet expected in the South Carolina surf zone and 5 to 7
feet expected in the Georgia surf zone.

* WHERE...South Carolina Beaches, and Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through this evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, from noon today to 2 PM EDT
Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The combination of strong northeast winds,
elevated tides and large breaking waves will increase the risk
for significant beach erosion during the high tide cycle late
this afternoon/early evening.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
